messages:
marta: Hey sec team — BlueCrest Q: they want confirmation we don't store customer PII in request logs and a list of who can access raw logs. Any quick notes I can paste back?

olivia: Short answer: we redact PII at ingest + access is RBAC with approvals. I can paste a short bullets list for them.

marta: Can you include exact fields/patterns we strip? They'll specifically ask about email / SSN / credit card numbers.

olivia: We strip known patterns (emails, SSNs, credit cards) and remove configured sensitive JSON keys at ingestion. Example redaction config we use internally: 
```
redaction:
  patterns:
    - email
    - ssn
    - credit_card
  json_keys:
    - user.email
    - payment.card_number
```

luke: Minor nuance: for embeddings pipeline we also HMAC identifiers before storage so raw IDs are never stored. @sam is that still accurate post-pipeline change?

sam: Yep — embeddings pipeline applies HMAC(key=service-key) to id fields before storing vectors. Access to raw logs is limited: infra & sec on a need-to-view basis, all via the infra-logs-access workflow (Jira INF-142).

isaac: Also call out subprocessors: we may share logs with cloud provider for debugging but only under DPA terms and with access logging/audit. Customers with stricter needs can opt for Private deployment.

marta: Can someone paste the exact 'who can access' wording? Customer wants roles/names rather than just 'infra & sec'.

olivia: Suggested wording: 
- SRE oncall (read-only access for incident triage)
- Infrastructure engineers (access granted with explicit approval)
- Security operations (audit and incident response)
Approvals require an IAM ticket + 2nd approver. Audit trail kept in Splunk (365d). Internal snippet: 
```
access_policy:
  allowed_roles:
    - sre:oncall
    - infra:engineer (approved)
    - security:ops
  approval: "IAM ticket + 2nd approver"
  audit: "all access logged in splunk (retention 365d)"
```

security-bot: Reminder: For customer-facing statements reference KB article https://redwood.internal/kb/logging-redaction v2.1 :information_source: 

marta: Thanks — I'll send back these bullets and the KB link. tagging legal for DPA/subprocessor confirmation: @nina

nina: Confirming: our standard DPA covers subprocessors listed in the annex. Customers can request an export of the subprocessor list. If they require different terms or on-prem, escalate to AE/team.

marta: :thumbsup: closing the loop — I'll reply to the customer now with these points and link to the KB.
